guard: the mesh handler's durable ask enforces the §6.5 contract and recovers by derivation: the shorthand is enforced (L4022), a non-conforming answer costs one attempt with its refusal bound for the answerer, attempts default to ONE and exhaust as the catchable L4006, the run driver's answer door reaches the CURRENT attempt's pause, and the discharge and adoption re-arm address the attempt actually armed, and the agent is told: each attempt is relayed to the seat as a turn under its own token (idempotent by goal id, carrying the schema and the previous refusal), an ask outside the roster refuses before an attempt opens, and a seat gone at the relay is L4002
why: Lane F durable-actions step 4 (2026-09-02): `ask` leaves the not-yet-durable seam and performs
as one checkpoint-plane pause per attempt, answered through the run driver's resolveCheckpoint.
Each contract half has a mutant: the spec's attempts default of ONE (MA1), the L4022 refusal of
an unreadable schema (MA2), the conformance check itself (MA3), the L4006 class (MA4), the
refusal reason bound for the answerer (MA5), the resolver accepting ask entries at all (MA6)
and addressing the CURRENT attempt's token (MA7), the discharge ending the attempt actually
armed (MA8), and the adoption re-arm inventory reading it the same way (MA9).
MA6 and MA7 mutate resolve-checkpoint.ts; the rest mutate mesh-handler.ts. Both are imported
by the suite through relative source paths — no build sits between the mutation and the run.
Batch B1 (2026-09-03) adds the relay: the seat is told over the same turn relay `turn` uses.
Each obligation has a mutant: the relay itself, its idempotency on re-entry, the roster gate,
the refusal carried on a re-ask, and the gone-seat classing.
Batch B2 (2026-09-03): the refusal is bound with its attempt, so a resume that re-relays
carries it; dropping it re-asked the seat with no reason its last answer failed.
